text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user states after a one-hour test drive that build quality and materials are high, and the interior beats his own Mercedes C-Class and is far ahead of a VW ID.3. Forum user states after a test drive that performance and chassis are at least at Mercedes level. Forum user states after a test drive that the controls are easy to use. Forum user states after a test drive that lane keeping worked fairly well. Forum user states after a test drive that the cameras are high resolution. Forum user likes that the tow hitch extends on its own and is rated for 2 tonnes. Forum user criticises that the rear bench does not fold down. Forum user criticises the small tailgate opening. Forum user calls the NOMI dashboard robot head a nice gimmick.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user states after a one-hour test drive that materials and finish are good. Forum user found consumption of about 24 kWh/100 km at 130 km/h in Eco at 10 degrees C acceptable. Forum user states the suspension is too soft in Eco and Normal, making it hard to hold a clean line on winding roads, while Sport modes are much better. Forum user finds power in Eco and Normal modes too weak, while Sport modes accelerate strongly. Forum user states NOMI only understood him in a quiet cabin, not while the radio was playing. Forum user wants a dedicated voice-control button. Forum user states the lane assist corrects constantly, making the steering wheel jitter. Forum user finds the boot small and impractical for a 5 m car, with no compartment for charging cables. Forum user criticises that there is no frunk. Forum user states the radio was offline most of the test drive, with no apparent internet connection. Forum user states the dealer staff were inexperienced with modern electric cars.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user who test-drove both cars and ordered the Tesla prefers its larger boot over the BYD Seal's. Forum user prefers the Tesla's larger frunk over the BYD Seal's. Forum user values that the Tesla has roof-load and towing ratings, which the BYD Seal lacks. Forum user chose the Tesla over the BYD Seal mainly for its lower consumption. Forum user values the Tesla's faster charging according to tests. Forum user values the Supercharger network. Forum user likes the rear touchscreen for the children. Forum user likes that the Tesla has no mandatory service intervals. Forum user dislikes the missing indicator stalk. Forum user dislikes the missing wiper stalk. Forum user misses ultrasonic parking sensors. Forum user sees the ambient lighting as a gimmick.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user (2020 Model 3 owner) states after a test drive of the new Model 3 Performance that the chassis is now on par with German makers. Forum user states after a test drive that the noise level is now on par with German makers. Forum user states tyre rolling noise at higher speeds is louder than in his older Model 3. Forum user praises the seat ventilation. Forum user finds the seats good overall. Forum user found the acceleration of the new Model 3 Performance impressive. Forum user states gear selection on the display worked without problems. Forum user found the indicator buttons very unusual and missed the signal at the first five roundabouts. Forum user states fan noise is audible when the audio is off. Forum user states the headrest sits further forward than in his 2020 car. Forum user states the brakes need high pedal force and bite less than expected. Forum user dislikes that the speed-warning beep must be disabled before every trip. Forum user wants a towbar; with the indicator buttons, its absence made the car not right for him yet.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user (2020 Model 3 owner) states after test-driving the new SR and Performance that he wants the ventilated seats. Forum user states the indicator button operation annoys him. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «das will ich haben»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a Model 3 Highland RWD Long Range reports about 722 km from a full charge with 43 km left, including Autopilot and up to 140 km/h, and says daily driving beats the displayed range. Owner likes the always-online browser for entertainment.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (company car, new since November 2024) states they are very happy with the EQE and finds much of the online criticism unfounded. Owner states the rear-wheel steering makes the car very manoeuvrable and recommends ordering it.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (EQE 300, built 11/2023) calls the front camera valuable because the view ahead over the bonnet is almost nil, and says the rear camera works well. Owner states the 360-degree camera greys out exactly the area closest to the car, which would be the most useful. Owner states they use the traffic-light camera view daily. Owner states the optional Burmester sound system is better than the standard one. Owner states the Digital Light projector headlights are worth having. Owner states the standard comfort suspension is excellent and air suspension is not needed. Owner states the boot is smaller than expected: a golf bag requires folding a rear seat section, and two golf bags the whole bench. Owner wishes they had 22 kW AC charging; their car has 11 kW because 22 kW was an extra-cost option. Owner wishes for front seat ventilation. Owner notes the upholstery is faux leather and wishes for genuine leather. Owner says they love the car and find the design beautiful despite online criticism. Owner (EQE 300, about one month and 3,500 km) reports more interior creaks and rattles than expected for Mercedes' quality standard, otherwise no failures. Owner finds acceleration good up to 120 km/h but sluggish above that despite 245 PS, attributing it to the S-Class-like weight.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user describing an EQE 300 (ownership not stated) praises a comfortable yet precise chassis well suited to long motorway trips. Forum user states the EQE has noticeably more interior space than the EQA or EQB. Forum user states charging power could be higher: the 400-volt architecture is mature and reliable but not fast.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (EQE 350+, bought used with 5,000 km, four weeks of ownership, switched from an Ioniq 5) describes the ride as like a flying carpet and does not regret the switch.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (A6 Avant e-tron quattro, experienced BEV driver) reports real motorway range above 450 km, doing two non-stop 404 km legs mostly at about 150 km/h on about 22.4 kWh/100 km. Owner reports charging 54.9 kWh from 9 % to 63 % in 13 minutes at an IONITY charger, briefly seeing 280 kW, with a charging curve better than expected. Owner rates the driver assistance as the best on the market: adaptive cruise, lane keeping and sign-based speed adaptation work well, with timely braking for limits and smooth acceleration. Owner names the missing overtaking (automatic lane-change) assistant as the only limitation of the assistance system. Owner finds the sign-based speed control often too slow for their taste. Same owner reports over 340 km of range in winter below -5 degrees C at average speeds above 120 km/h.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user who drove an A6 e-tron (not owned) enjoyed it and considers Audi's assistance systems a current reference, worth paying extra for on the motorway.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Forum user who drove two A6 e-tron workshop loan cars says Audi is no longer premium except in its prices.
